My personal favorite was when one of the longshore guys smelled something burning and evacuated the rest of the union, but there wasn’t a general evacuation alarm for the whole facility. And then when ops heard about it they spent two hours investigating to determine the source and severity.

There’s rules on the books that if there are fires on the beach down by our docks we had to put the elevator into shutdown mode. We were not at an isolated facility by the way. We were next to some major shipping ports on a major river. I won’t deny ops the right to do some investigation, but when I heard over the radio “yeah, I do smell something” that should have been when 911 got called. 

Two hours after the first people were evac’d (and let me tell you, our evac zone was still way too close) we had over a dozen fire trucks pouring into the facility and getting into their staging positions. Fire Department sent over three chiefs and the media spokesman to handle the journalists. We got a couple helicopters in the sky too.

So yeah, fire in a grain elevator is bad news and our control room did not respect how serious of a problem that could be.
